angles: The Acceptance Rate Illusion: Marketing vs Reality — vendor marketing cites 80%+ but real enterprise data shows 27-35% acceptance, exposing a fundamental gap between marketing metrics and production reality

The Quality Paradox: You Feel Productive But You're Slower — developers report feeling 20% faster while actually being 19% slower due to review overhead and debugging, showing acceptance rate measures feelings not outcomes

The Inverse Expertise Problem — best developers have the lowest acceptance rates because they critically evaluate suggestions, while the least experienced accept blindly, making high acceptance rate a red flag not a success signal
The Perverse Incentive Trap — when acceptance rate becomes a target metric, teams optimize for clicking Tab faster rather than code quality, creating systemic degradation of review culture
The Hidden Security Tax — 92% of AI codebases contain critical vulnerabilities, but high acceptance rates mask this accumulating security debt until it becomes a production incident

The 80% Problem — AI excels at the obvious 80% of code but consistently misses the critical 20%: rate limiting, observability, error handling, security hardening — the parts that determine production survival
Code Survival Rate: The Metric That Actually Matters — AI code has 65% survival rate vs 92% for human code, meaning developers accept and then silently replace AI suggestions at much higher rates

Review Fatigue: The Human Bottleneck That Acceptance Rate Ignores — high acceptance creates review pipeline pressure that causes 91% longer review times and reviewer fatigue leading to rubber-stamping

The Post-Acceptance Rewrite Problem — high acceptance rate doesn't mean code is production-ready; developers often accept to avoid disrupting flow and then rewrite immediately, a 'silent rejection' invisible to metrics
DORA Metrics: The Alternative Framework — deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, and MTTR measure what actually matters vs acceptance rate which measures only AI tool usage
